title: Acceptance-language characterization
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean word, and let $S$ be a natural number. Suppose $N$ uses at most $sp(m)$ space on every input of length $m$, and $sp(\lvert x\rvert)\le S$. If a configuration $C$ on input $x$ is reachable from the initial configuration by some sequence of choice bits, then the encoding of $x$, the configuration code of $C$ at space bound $S$, and $S$ belongs to the acceptance language of $N$ if and only if $C$ is halted and its output is exactly the one-bit word $[1]$.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ uses at most $sp(m)$ space on every input of length $m$
